name: Bamboo-tube rice
summary: Glutinous rice grilled in a bamboo tube, a Ba Na and Xơ Đăng dish Go Vietnam serves with grilled chicken. Three Go Vietnam figures for a tube do not match. All three stay.
origin: Go Vietnam calls cơm lam Kon Tum a dish of the Ba Na and Xơ Đăng, often at community festivals, served with grilled chicken.
howToEat: Go Vietnam’s cơm lam article says rinse glutinous rice, pack it into fresh green bamboo with a little water, seal it with banana leaf, and prop it by charcoal for 30–60 minutes. Peel the charred bark, keep the thin membrane, and eat it hot with sesame salt, peanut salt, grilled meat, or free-range chicken.

The Kon Tum cluster article is more specific. Khẩu Cẩm glutinous rice from Ba Na hamlets around Kon Tum goes into fresh bamboo with stream water and grills for an hour. Eat it with black sesame salt and stir-fried chicken. That article prints 30,000–50,000 VND a tube.

The grilled-chicken article prints 20,000–30,000 VND a tube. The general cơm lam article prints a common 2025 range of about 10,000–25,000 VND a tube depending on size and region, and names Pleiku market and the road toward Buôn Ma Thuột, not a Kon Tum stall. The three figures stay. Check on arrival.
where: Ba Na hamlets around Kon Tum, including a village lunch at Kon K’Tu on the cluster article, and community festivals. Măng Đen is the other place the grilled-chicken article names for the same pairing.
seoTitle: Com lam in Kon Tum — bamboo-tube rice
seoDescription: Ba Na and Xơ Đăng sticky rice grilled in bamboo and eaten with chicken. Go Vietnam prints 30,000–50,000, 20,000–30,000, and a highland 10,000–25,000 VND a tube.
